base.description: The PDU as it ships, with GMT fuses fitted.

description: Server Technology PRO1 -48VDC Switched PDU, Primary unit, 2U. It has two input blocks, A and B, each with three stud pairs for +RTN, GND and -48VDC. It has 16 screw-down outputs in four green blocks, with GMT fuses. The rear carries the controller plate with Ethernet, serial, link and two sensor jacks. Each input takes up to 100 A, and the box is rated 200 A at -48 V.

gaps.note: the 16 output screw-down terminals are drawn as art in four green blocks. The registry holds no key for a high-density screw-down block and no document held prints its pitch or its maker, so no connector part and no mate exist. The data sheet and the guide say bare stripped wire, 14 AWG at most.
gaps.wanted: a drawing of the output block with its pitch, or the block's maker part number.

gaps.note: the two temperature and humidity inputs TAM1 and TAM2 are 4P4C jacks. The registry's rj11 note says the four-position jack is another interface, and no key exists for it, so both are drawn as art.
gaps.wanted: a registry key for the 4P4C jack, and the probe cable's connector.

gaps.note: no drawing of the rear is held. The plate, its jacks and the perforated field are estimated from a photograph of the sibling 4811. The Link variant's rear plate, in Detail A of the drawing, is not modelled here.
gaps.wanted: a rear drawing of this model, or a straight-on photograph of its rear.

gaps.note: the drawing shows the ear at the rear for Option B and gives no distance from the faceplate. The drawing labels the bracket MB-0005-0026 on both options but names no kit, and the data sheet says only "mounting brackets included" and points to the Mounting Bracket Guide, which is not held. The held PDU Mounting Solutions data sheet lists 2U horizontal 19 in. L-bracket kits (for example KIT-MB2U-4B, bracket MB-0005-0026-20) for the PRO2, PRO3X and PRO4X families; it does not name this model, so no document held ties the bracket to a kit and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: the Mounting Bracket Guide, or a statement of which bracket kit ships with this model.

gaps.note: lamps A and B and the lamp over each output are drawn as lit green in the sibling photograph. The guide on PDF page 206 says a lit output lamp means power is supplied; it gives no meaning for lamps A and B, so no state is stated for them.
gaps.wanted: the PRO1 DC User Guide section on the input lamps.

name: pro1-48dcwc-16-2x100-a0

chassis.note: datasheet - "3.5in tall x 17.0in wide x 12.0in deep [89mm x 432mm x 305mm]". The drawing gives the body as 432.00 wide, 304.80 deep and 88.00 high, and 482.00 over the ears, so the body is modelled at 432.0 by 88.0 by 304.8, the drawing's figures. The data sheet's 89 is the same 3.5 in, rounded.

colours.note: estimated by eye from the sibling 4811's front and rear photographs (same layout); no pixel count was taken: the body is black, the output blocks are green with black latch ears, the input blocks are black under clear covers and the lamps are green. On the rear plate the SER and NET jack housings read white and the LNK and the two TAM jacks black. The photographs are of another model, so the colours are the sibling's.

ears.note: The drawing shows two ways to fit the included brackets, labelled MB-0005-0026 on both options, Option A at the front and Option B at the rear, with 482.00 over the ears, 455.80 minimum and 469.00 maximum, the ear slots 44.50 and 76.30 from the centre line. Option A puts the ears flush with the faceplate. Option B puts them at the rear; no figure gives how far back, so no `at` is written for it (gaps: rack-ears). Neither the drawing nor the guide says which option ships, so neither is marked as the default.

front.note: drawing - the plan view. From the left: input block A (43.9 by 76.5, 9.4 from the left edge and 5.8 from the top), a perforated field, the lamp and letter A, two output blocks one above the other, the centre perforated field with the maker's address label, two more output blocks, a perforated field, the letter and lamp B, and input block B, which mirrors A. Every position was read from the raster at 3.3 px/mm and carries about 1 mm. The face is symmetric about the centre line to within the reading.

inputs.note: datasheet - "(2) x 1/4-20 dual-studs on 5/8 in. centers (100A max)", 200 A, 9.6 kW at -48 V. The (2) counts the two input blocks, not studs: the PRO1 DC User Guide (301-4800-3), PDF page 206 (printed 206 of 211), says each block holds three terminal positions, and its PDF page 9 figure shows three dual-stud rows in a block. The studs stand 15.875 apart as that line says. The PRO1 DC User Guide (301-4800-3), PDF page 9 (printed 9 of 211), "Terminal Stud Spacing", labels the same spacing 16.0 in its figure, a 0.125 difference that the data sheet's inch figure settles. The legends read +RTN, GND and -48VDC from the top, on the plan view.

method.note: FIGURES FROM A RASTER DRAWING. Server Technology data sheet 48DCWC-16-2X100-A0 (Primary) and 48DCXC-16-2X100-A0 (Link), PDF page 4 "Drawings", is a 748 ppi raster (extracted with pdfimages). Its plan view was read at 3.3 px/mm, the scale that puts the 432.00 body on the view, with the origin at the body's top left. A raster carries about 1 mm, so every figure read from it is that good and no better. The sibling model 4811, which has the same layout, was photographed from the front and the rear; those photographs give colours and counts only. No photograph or drawing is copied here.

outputs.note: datasheet and drawing - "(16) x Screw-down terminals (10A max)", four blocks of four outputs. The wiring drawing on PDF page 4 of the data sheet labels the upper left block FUSE A1 to A4 and the lower left block FUSE A5 to A8, with B1 to B8 on the right, so each block carries four numerals.

rear.note: estimated - no drawing held shows the rear, only the photograph of the sibling 4811. The controller plate is placed 13.5 from the left and 40 from the top, 134 by 44, and the perforated field at 152 to 405 across, moved right of the plate where the photograph's angle overlaps them and 14 to 70 down, each read as a fraction of the face off that photograph. The photograph looks from one side, so these carry several millimetres (gaps: rear-plate).

sides.note: drawing - the side view gives the depth as 304.80 and the height as 88.00. Six screw holes stand on a 50.80 pitch, 25.40 from each end, 45 from the top. The perforated band runs about 22 from the front to 19 from the rear and lies 8 to 36 below the top. The left side is the right's mirror.

top-bottom.note: estimated - the iso view on PDF page 4 shows the top as plain sheet with a few screw heads near the edges. Nothing is drawn on the top or the bottom, which no drawing held shows.
